headline: Geopolitical Fog and Jobs Data Cloud a Cautious Friday Open
body_html:
Markets head into Friday's open carrying the weight of Thursday's bruising session, when declining issues outnumbered advancers 347 to 201 across a universe of 549 names. Consumer and homebuilder stocks bore the brunt of the selling, dropping 2.64% and 2.39% respectively, while energy and semiconductors managed slim gains of 0.66% and 0.54% — the only sectors to finish in positive territory. The lopsided breadth underscores a market searching for footing amid overlapping macro risks.

The morning's most consequential catalyst arrives with the U.S. jobs report, which traders are already pricing against a backdrop of a firmer dollar and gold on pace for its best weekly advance since January. Oil markets remain unsettled as vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has thinned noticeably, with Iran-Oman diplomatic talks drawing close attention from energy desks. President Trump's comments suggesting the conflict with Iran could wind down soon offered some relief, though analysts caution that any resolution timeline remains fluid.

On the geopolitical front, a trilateral defence agreement among Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan is expected to be formalised in Riyadh on Friday, adding another variable to an already complex regional picture. A Houthi strike wounding eleven civilians inside Saudi Arabia complicates the diplomatic backdrop heading into the weekend. Traders will watch whether energy prices extend Thursday's gains at the open, and whether the jobs print resets rate expectations before U.S. equities resume trading.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Traffic Slows as Diplomacy Hangs in the Balance
briefs.body: Shipping movement through the Strait of Hormuz has declined markedly this week as Iran-Oman negotiations continue. The uncertainty is keeping a floor under crude prices, with oil rising Thursday on concerns about the timeline for any formal reopening of the critical waterway. Energy desks are treating the talks as the single most important near-term supply variable.

briefs.headline: Gold on Track for Best Weekly Gain Since January
briefs.body: Bullion is headed for its strongest weekly performance in more than six months as safe-haven demand builds around Middle East instability and the approaching U.S. payrolls release. The dollar has simultaneously firmed, an unusual pairing that reflects the depth of geopolitical anxiety. Friday's jobs data could break that correlation in either direction.

briefs.headline: Trilateral Defence Pact to Be Signed in Riyadh
briefs.body: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan are set to formalise a joint defence agreement in Riyadh on Friday, according to sources cited by Reuters. The deal arrives amid elevated regional tensions following a Houthi strike on Saudi territory that wounded eleven civilians. Analysts say the pact signals a broader realignment of security partnerships across the Middle East and South Asia.

briefs.headline: Sweetgreen Trims Annual Outlook on Food-Safety Scare
briefs.body: The fast-casual salad chain lowered its full-year guidance after a cyclospora contamination scare weighed on customer traffic and same-store sales trends. The revision adds to pressure on consumer-facing names, a sector already down 2.64% in Thursday's session. Management indicated recovery will depend on restoring consumer confidence in the coming weeks.

briefs.headline: Virginia Governor Steps Into NextEra-Dominion Merger Talks
briefs.body: Virginia's governor signalled plans to intervene in the proposed merger between NextEra and Dominion, citing concerns that the combination could push electricity rates higher for state residents. The move introduces a significant regulatory hurdle for a deal that had been advancing through approvals. Utility investors will watch closely for any formal filing ahead of the weekend.

briefs.headline: Thursday's Sharpest Losers Signal Earnings-Season Reckoning
briefs.body: Several names posted severe single-session drops in Thursday's trading, led by Universal Technical Institute off 34.22%, LegalZoom down 30.06%, and Datadog shedding 19.03%. Dutch Bros and Celsius Holdings each fell roughly 18-19%. The concentrated damage across consumer, software, and IT-services names points to earnings disappointments driving sector-wide sentiment ahead of Friday's macro data.
